title: Treasure hunt: coordinates
reflection: Byte found treasure it couldn't see, with just some numbers. Where are coordinates like these used in real life (maps, GPS, battleships)? Why did Byte need variables to get home?

steps.goal: MINE has buried a treasure (a gold block) in the ground near Byte, in a new place every time. mine.challenge() says where: so many blocks forward, then so many to the right. Bring Byte right on top of it.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: Byte has to stop right on top of the treasure.
hints: local forward, right = mine.challenge() puts the two numbers in two variables. mine.say them to see them!
for i = 1, forward do byte.forward() end, then byte.turnRight(), then the same with right.
block_hints: "the challenge's number 1" is how far forward, "the challenge's number 2" how far to the right. Keep them in two variables (Variables, "set ... to").
"repeat" with the variable forward in it: "move forward". Then "turn right", and the same with right.

steps.goal: Now dig the treasure up (Byte digs the block under it with byte.digDown()) and bring Byte back home, where it started.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: dig up the treasure, then bring Byte back where it started.
hints: Your variables still remember how far Byte went: they are the way home too.
After byte.digDown(): right times byte.back(), byte.turnLeft(), forward times byte.back().
block_hints: Your variables still remember how far Byte went: they are the way home too.
After "dig below": "repeat" right times "move back", "turn left", "repeat" forward times "move back".

steps.goal: Three treasures! mine.challenge() gives 6 numbers: forward and right of the first, of the second, of the third. Dig them all up and come back home. Byte has to remember where it is.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: dig up all three treasures, then bring Byte back where it started.
hints: Two variables, f and r, say where Byte is (they start at 0). A function goTo(toF, toR) moves Byte there: while f < toF go forward and add 1 to f; while f > toF go back and take 1 away; then the same to the right.
for i = 1, 3 do goTo(mine.challenge(2 * i - 1), mine.challenge(2 * i)) byte.digDown() end, then goTo(0, 0) brings Byte home.
block_hints: Two variables, f and r, say where Byte is (start them at 0). In Functions, make "goTo" with two inputs, toF and toR: "repeat while f < toF": "move forward", "change f by 1"; "repeat while f > toF": "move back", "change f by -1"; then the same to the right.
Call goTo with "the challenge's number 1" and "2", then "dig below"; then with 3 and 4, and 5 and 6. Last, goTo 0, 0 brings Byte home.
